prompt: Tenant Priya's lease on a Boulder duplex gives her a right of first refusal. The owner, Glen, receives a $640,000 offer from an investor and accepts it, subject to Priya's right. What may Priya do?

options.text: Force Glen to sell to her at a price fixed in her lease
Purchase on the same terms the investor offered
Cancel her lease without penalty because of the sale
Block the sale to the investor for the rest of her lease term

explanation: A right of first refusal lets the holder buy if and when the owner decides to sell, by matching a bona fide third-party offer. Glen chose to sell at $640,000, so Priya may buy on those terms or let the investor's deal go ahead. An option, by contrast, lets the holder buy at a preset price whenever she elects during the option period.

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an option contract, which fixes a price in advance. A right of first refusal ties her price to the outside offer.
distractorExplanations.c: A sale does not end an existing lease; the buyer takes title subject to Priya's tenancy, and the right gives her no penalty-free exit.
distractorExplanations.d: The right lets her match, not veto. If she declines to match, Glen may complete the sale to the investor.
